scope.description: Re-run the extended-window case with the demoted peer's log position recorded at the same moment its own configuration view is recorded, so the divergence can be attributed to the entry not arriving or to it not being processed.
assumptions: Same construction as the fixed extended-window experiment: only the leader bootstrapped, per-node timing (leader 20s, near 6s, far voters 3s), DemoteVoter for the near node, transport routes removed in both directions between those two nodes and the two far voters.
The near node's view and indices are read in the same breath, after the far nodes report the demotion, so a lag in one cannot be an artefact of reading the other later.
The leader's LastIndex at that moment is the configuration entry's index, two entries above the bootstrap configuration and the no-op.
excluded: No partition healing, no snapshots and no client traffic besides the membership change.
No production code or default is modified.

basis.prefix: Four nodes are created, wired fully connected and started with the bootstrapped leader holding the four-voter configuration; the harness waits for that leader, calls DemoteVoter on the near node and waits until both far nodes report it without a vote. It then reads the leader's configuration, the near node's own view of its suffrage with a bounded three second settle loop, and in the same emission the near node's LastIndex, commit and applied index and state plus the leader's LastIndex as the configuration index, from which it derives view_old_and_log_complete and view_old_and_log_short. After that it partitions the two nodes off from the far voters and runs the two VerifyLeader calls and the write as before.

semantic_changes: Per-node timing instead of one shared Config: bootstrapped leader HeartbeatTimeout=ElectionTimeout=LeaderLeaseTimeout=20s; the two far voters 3s; the near node 6s (all ValidateConfig-clean).

before.description: Extend the observation window of the non-voter VerifyLeader defect: cut a long-lease leader off from the voter majority while one non-voter stays reachable, ask VerifyLeader immediately, then ask again once the majority has elected a competing leader and committed a write.
assumptions: Real target constructors and APIs: BootstrapCluster, NewRaft, DemoteVoter, VerifyLeader, Apply, GetConfiguration; per-node Config values only, no production code or default changed.

Only the leader is bootstrapped with the four-server configuration (all voters), so it is the only node that can campaign initially; the other nodes start with empty configurations and adopt the configuration through normal AppendEntries replication.

The near node's voter-to-non-voter transition is the public DemoteVoter call; the harness waits until the far side reports it without a vote and records the leader's own view of that suffrage separately from the near node's self view.
Partition is imposed by removing in-memory transport routes in both directions between {leader, near} and the two far voters; the far voters keep their mutual routes.
The 20s leader lease is within ValidateConfig (LeaderLeaseTimeout <= HeartbeatTimeout) and only makes the pre-existing window observable; the defect claim does not rest on the value chosen.
excluded: No TCP or cross-host partition; no disk-backed log/snapshot store.
No change to the target's defaults, and no instrumentation of internal counters.

prefix.before: Four nodes are created first (identity is the in-memory transport address), then wired fully connected and started; only the first node is bootstrapped with the configuration {leader, near, far1, far2} all Voter, so it wins the initial election and replicates the configuration to the others (they start empty and cannot campaign). The harness waits for the bootstrapped node to be Leader, then for the treatment calls DemoteVoter(near) and waits until both far nodes report the near node without a vote. It emits a setup CA_EVENT carrying the leader's configuration summary (voters, nonvoters, quorum_size, near_node_voter from the leader's view, near_node_self_voter) and the per-node timings. It then removes the transport routes between {leader, near} and {far1, far2} in both directions, emits a partition event, and calls the public VerifyLeader on the partitioned leader (3s deadline for the treatment, 45s for the control). It polls the two far nodes for a Leader state for up to 15s; if one appears it emits verify_while_superseded with the second VerifyLeader result plus both nodes' states, applies 'assurance-superseded-write' through the competing leader, and emits stale_write with the applied index, the state of both FSMs and the old leader's state. The control repeats the identical construction and timing without the demotion.
prefix.after: Four nodes are created, wired fully connected and started with the bootstrapped leader holding the four-voter configuration; the harness waits for that leader, calls DemoteVoter on the near node and waits until both far nodes report it without a vote. It then reads the leader's configuration, the near node's own view of its suffrage with a bounded three second settle loop, and in the same emission the near node's LastIndex, commit and applied index and state plus the leader's LastIndex as the configuration index, from which it derives view_old_and_log_complete and view_old_and_log_short. After that it partitions the two nodes off from the far voters and runs the two VerifyLeader calls and the write as before.

requirement.before: A success from VerifyLeader is a confirmation that the caller may keep treating this node as leader and read its FSM (api.go:880-882 documents that purpose). Since non-voters are, by the target's own definition, 'not considered for elections or commitment purposes' (configuration.go:16-18), the confirmation must rest on acknowledgements from a quorum of voters; a non-voter's acknowledgement may not substitute for one.

responsibility.before: Leader-side quorum confirmation consumed by clients through VerifyLeader, and the leader-lease step-down path that is supposed to bound how long such a confirmation can be wrong.

before.description: The partitioned long-lease leader, able to reach only the demoted non-voter, answers VerifyLeader with success before any competitor exists.

Decisive extension of the anomaly: the same confirmation succeeds again while a competing leader already holds leadership on the voter-majority side, i.e. the confirmation outlives the election the lease is supposed to bound.

A write committed by the competing leader is absent from the old leader's FSM while that old leader still reports Leader, i.e. a client that gates reads on the confirmed leadership reads state missing a committed write.
Control with identical per-node timing but the near node still a voter: the far side is a minority, so no competitor can appear and the same call must not report success.
